faq.q1: Why would a seller sell without a profit?
faq.a1: Because the alternative is worse. Returning the unit to the developer typically deducts 10–15% of the full unit price and refunds the remainder over years. Transferring without overprice returns all of what they paid, in cash, on completion.
faq.a2: The unit at an older contract price, below the developer's price today, continuing the normal installments. That price difference is their gain from the day they sign, without paying an overprice to anyone.
faq.q3: How do I know the numbers are real?
faq.a3: Before an opportunity appears, the contract and payment receipts are read, reconciled and confirmed by a human analyst. Every figure displayed carries a marker showing whether it is confirmed by documents or still estimated.
faq.q4: What if I have overdue installments?
faq.a4: They are calculated within the assessment, and the deal terms state who settles them — usually the buyer, as part of what is required from them. Acting early, before default procedures escalate, matters.
faq.a5: No. Aqary deals directly with the unit owner and directly with the end buyer. Signing and official dealings with the developer happen in your own name, with your attendance; Aqary prepares the file and follows the process through.
faq.a6: The seller pays nothing — 0% commission. The buyer pays a {pct}% success fee, charged only when the assignment actually completes. The developer's own assignment fee is separate, set by the developer's policy, and shown on every opportunity before you make an offer.
faq.q7: What happens if the transfer does not complete?
faq.a7: The success fee is charged on completion only, so if the assignment does not go through, it is not charged. Any reservation deposit follows the terms recorded in the deal room before it is paid, and every step of the deal is documented there for both sides.
faq.a8: The developer does, always. Aqary does not approve assignments and cannot override a developer's rules. We prepare the file to the developer's stated requirements, show its published conditions on every opportunity, and follow the process through — but the approval and the NOC are the developer's decision.
faq.noPromiseBody: Aqary presents estimates based on real documents, but makes no promise of a specific selling period or a guaranteed recovery percentage. The outcome depends on the contract, the developer's approval and the market.

developers.heroTitle: Turn payment distress into contract continuity.
developers.heroSub: When a holder stops paying, an assignment replaces them with a qualified buyer who continues the same schedule at the same contractual price. Collection continues. The unit is not reclaimed, not repriced, and not resold.
developers.outcomesTitle: What an assignment changes for you.
developers.outcome1Title: A paying account instead of a distressed one
developers.outcome1Body: The contract keeps its original price and schedule. You replace a holder who has stopped paying, rather than reclaiming a unit and carrying it back into inventory.
developers.outcome2Body: Every buyer reaching your assignment desk has passed identity checks and declared a financial profile, and every figure on the file has been confirmed by a human analyst against documents.
developers.outcome3Body: Holders state why they are exiting at intake. Aggregated across your projects, that is an early read on where payment stress is building in your backlog.
developers.workflowTitle: Where you sit in the process.
developers.workflow1Sub: Contract, receipts and statement verified by an Aqary analyst.
developers.workflow2Sub: Identity checked and financial capacity recorded before any offer.
developers.workflow3Sub: The complete file reaches your desk against your own stated requirements.
developers.workflow4Sub: You approve, reject, or ask for more. Aqary cannot proceed without you.
developers.workflow5Sub: Signed in the developer's own process, with both parties present.
developers.controlSub: Aqary does not approve assignments. It records your published policy, applies it before a contract can be listed, and shows it to every buyer.
